scheme_name: Supply of Kadaknath Chicks on Subsidy
description:
The Supply of Kadaknath Chicks on Subsidy scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to promote the rearing of Kadaknath poultry. 

This scheme aims to enhance the livelihood of rural households by providing them with a sustainable source of income through poultry farming. 

Kadaknath is a breed of chicken native to the Madhya Pradesh region of India. 

The Kadaknath chicken is known for its unique black meat and high nutritional value. 

The scheme was officially launched in 2018 as part of the government's broader efforts to promote indigenous breeds of livestock. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to farmers and rural households for the purchase of Kadaknath chicks. 

The government aims to distribute a total of 2.5 million Kadaknath chicks under this scheme over a period of five years. 

Each beneficiary is eligible to receive a subsidy for up to 50 chicks. 

The subsidy amount is set at ₹70 per chick. 

This means that a beneficiary can receive a total subsidy of ₹3,500 for the maximum number of chicks. 

The scheme also aims to promote the nutritional benefits of Kadaknath chicken, which is rich in protein and low in cholesterol. 

The target beneficiaries of the scheme include small and marginal farmers, women self-help groups, and rural households. 

To be eligible for the subsidy, applicants must be at least 18 years old. 

There is no specific upper age limit for eligibility. 

The income criteria for eligibility are set at an annual income of less than ₹1 lakh. 

This income limit is aimed at supporting economically weaker sections of society. 

The application process for the scheme involves several steps. 

First, interested beneficiaries must approach the local Animal Husbandry Department. 

They need to fill out an application form provided by the department. 

The application form requires basic details such as name, age, address, and income. 

Beneficiaries must also provide proof of identity and income. 

Documents required include an Aadhaar card, income certificate, and a passport-sized photograph. 

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the officials of the Animal Husbandry Department. 

After verification, the beneficiaries are informed about their eligibility status. 

If approved, the beneficiaries receive a subsidy amount directly into their bank accounts. 

The disbursement of the subsidy is typically done within 30 days of approval. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is particularly beneficial for women as it encourages their participation in poultry farming. 

Women self-help groups are specifically targeted to empower them economically. 

The Kadaknath breed is also known for its resilience to diseases, making it easier for farmers to rear. 

The government has set a target to train at least 10,000 farmers in poultry management practices over the next three years. 

Training sessions cover aspects such as feeding, housing, and health management of Kadaknath chickens. 

The scheme also aims to create awareness about the health benefits of consuming Kadaknath chicken. 

The nutritional profile of Kadaknath chicken includes higher protein content compared to regular broiler chickens. 

Kadaknath chicken contains about 25% protein and only 2% fat. 

This makes it a preferred choice for health-conscious consumers. 

The government has also initiated marketing support for Kadaknath chicken to enhance its marketability. 

This includes branding and promoting Kadaknath chicken as a premium product. 

The scheme is expected to generate employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It is projected that the scheme will create around 100,000 jobs in the poultry sector. 

The government has allocated ₹50 crores for the implementation of this scheme over the next five years. 

This funding is aimed at supporting the distribution of chicks and training programs. 

The scheme is part of the larger National Livestock Mission which aims to promote sustainable livestock development. 

The National Livestock Mission was launched in 2014 to enhance livestock productivity. 

The Supply of Kadaknath Chicks on Subsidy scheme aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme is also expected to contribute to the overall economic development of rural areas. 

By promoting indigenous breeds, the government aims to preserve biodiversity. 

Kadaknath chickens are known for their adaptability to local climatic conditions. 

This makes them a suitable choice for rural households in various regions of India. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have reported increased income. 

Many beneficiaries have expressed satisfaction with the ease of the application process. 

The government continues to monitor the implementation of the scheme to ensure its effectiveness. 

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate the impact on beneficiaries' livelihoods. 

The Supply of Kadaknath Chicks on Subsidy scheme is a significant step towards promoting self-sufficiency in rural India. 

It empowers farmers to take control of their livelihoods through sustainable poultry farming. 

The scheme not only supports economic growth but also promotes health and nutrition among rural populations. 

In conclusion, the Supply of Kadaknath Chicks on Subsidy scheme is a comprehensive initiative aimed at enhancing the livelihoods of rural households through poultry farming. 

It provides financial assistance and training to ensure the successful rearing of Kadaknath chickens. 

The scheme is a vital part of India's efforts to promote indigenous livestock breeds and improve rural economies.
